value.reason: The data-export endpoint (server.ts:660, POST /rest/user/data-export) takes the logged-in user's email and replaces every vowel with '*' (routes/dataExport.ts:22). It then fetches orders using only that masked string (routes/dataExport.ts:33). The masking loses information, so different emails can end up as the same key. For example, a user who registers an address that differs from the victim's only in its vowels would get the same key and receive the victim's orders in their export. The orders collection is seeded with the email as its owner field (data/datacreator.ts:798), and the evidence shows no second check: no user ID, no hash prefix, and no collision guard like the one in the negative example. Nothing confirms that the returned orders belong to the requester, so other users' personal and order data can leak through a public endpoint. This is an object-level authorization flaw built on a user-influenced, lossy key.
